newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BT says no decision on TNT stake.
newsitem.headline: BT says no decision on TNT stake.

text.p: Bankers Trust Australia Ltd said on Wednesday it had made no decision about accepting the takeover bid for TNT Ltd by Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV.
"BT has not committed itself to any course of action. There are no further developments," BT Australian equities chief Rohan Hedley said in a statement prepared for Reuters.
BT has a 19.99 percent stake in the Australian-based international transport firm, enough to block the A$2.0 billion friendly bid by KPN as it wants at least 90 percent control.
A BT spokeswoman said Hedley did not have a view on TNT's first quarter results issued earlier on Wednesday which showed a 14.7 percent rise in operating profit to A$27.0 million.
BT, an investment bank and funds manager, raised its stake in TNT from 16.0 percent soon after KPN announced its agreed A$2.45 a share bid on October 2. KPN has 19.8 percent of TNT.
BT's purchases led to local share market speculation that it could be seeking a rival bidder which would be interested in TNT's lucrative European-based express freight division.

TNT chairman Fred Millar told reporters on Wednesday that he had not spoken to BT since it increased its holding, but did not see a rival bid on the horizon. Millar, speaking after the annual meeting, said he believed the KPN bid would succeed.
A corporate source told Reuters that KPN executive Ad Scheepbouwer was likely to return to Australia before the bid closed in just under two weeks.
The source said he could not say if Scheepbouwer, the head of KPN's PTT Post division, would meet Hedley or other investment executives from Bankers Trust.
